## Overview

Formulated rigorously by George Stigler in *The Theory of Economic Regulation* (1971), **Regulatory Capture** occurs when the regulatory process is commandeered by incumbent firms to serve their own profitability and stifle competition, rather than protecting consumers or the environment.

## Mechanisms of Capture

1. **Information Asymmetry:** Regulators depend on technical data provided by the regulated industry itself, creating cognitive and epistemic bias.
2. **The Revolving Door:** Officials oscillate between public regulatory roles and lucrative corporate executive or lobbying positions, aligning their career incentives with industry favor.
3. **Regulatory Moats & Licensing:** Incumbent industry players actively lobby for complex, burdensome regulations that large incumbents can easily absorb but which effectively bankrupt small startups and prevent entry.

## Relation to Economic & Policy Paradigms

Rooted in [[public-choice-theory]], regulatory capture explains why well-intentioned regulatory statutes frequently lead to monopolistic market distortions. In complex compliance frameworks, metrics intended to monitor safety or honesty are frequently gamed, illustrating [[goodharts-law]].
